title: Next.js App Router cache: a real support discussion with changing advice
selection: 19 manually selected public source records: 18 comments from one coherent issue plus its linked implementation PR. Selection was made before showcase retrieval runs. This is a curated case study, not an unbiased benchmark sample.

temporal_policy.name: conservative-current-snapshot-availability
temporal_policy.observed_at_rule: max(created_at, updated_at); current body is never assumed available before its last recorded update.
temporal_policy.meaning: Phases order the available current snapshots. They do not reconstruct unavailable original revisions. Original publication dates in paraphrases are narrative attribution only.
temporal_policy.warning: Most January-to-May comments were updated on August 10. Earlier historical queries cannot use these current bodies. The mutable issue opening body is excluded entirely.

phases.title: Issue closed in favor of discussion

events.author: feedthejim
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: PR 48383, authored by feedthejim and merged on April 21, changes App Router client caching. Its description distinguishes default prefetch, disabled prefetch and full prefetch. Disabled prefetch stops speculative fetching but still allows a recently visited page to be reused for thirty seconds. The description lists possible future page cache lifetime controls and hover prefetch as follow-up ideas, not shipped configuration options.

events.author: Fredkiss3
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In a January 11 comment, Fredkiss3 reports an experiment in which adding a query string to a Link appears to cause repeated server navigation while retaining the initial prefetch. The author links a reproduction and describes changed scroll behavior. This is an experimental workaround report, not a documented API guarantee.

events.author: Fredkiss3
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In a January 16 follow-up, Fredkiss3 limits the earlier query-string workaround: different URLs within the same dynamic segment can still reuse cached results after their first visit. Random values could force new URLs but risk hydration mismatch. A stable useId avoids that mismatch yet permits reuse again. The earlier observation does not establish that every query-string Link refetches.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In a February 20 reply, timneutkens says the appropriate Link and refresh behavior is still being discussed, including mutations. Adding unit tests records current behavior and helps router development; it does not announce a permanent decision to retain that behavior. The reply acknowledges feedback and describes other ongoing router work.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In an April 5 update, timneutkens says the client-side router cache is being reworked and that more information will follow. This announces ongoing work without publishing a complete API or claiming that all reported cases are fixed.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In another April 5 reply, timneutkens corrects the claim that refreshing leaves other router pages untouched: router.refresh() in the canary version invalidates the entire router cache. The author says using it is acceptable for the time being. This statement is explicitly about the canary behavior discussed then.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In an April 11 review of a linked reproduction, timneutkens identifies a variable shared at module scope between requests as the source of session drift. The example also changes session state while rendering a layout. The reply distinguishes those application issues from the router complaint and suggests middleware for the relevant side effect. It does not prove that every stale-data report has that cause.

events.author: grantmagdanz
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On May 16, grantmagdanz reports a recurring interactive workflow: visit page A, perform an action on page B, then return to A within thirty seconds and see old data. Their team spent nearly a day investigating mutation and cache handling while trying to adopt the app directory. The comment asks for an update or workaround.

events.author: Fredkiss3
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In response on May 16, Fredkiss3 describes version-dependent behavior. Before 13.3.2, disabling Link prefetch could avoid the reported stale-data behavior, at a navigation-speed cost; 13.3.1 is suggested as a temporary downgrade. In newer behavior, prefetch=false prevents speculative loading but still reuses the client cache. The reply links PR 48383 and describes configurable page cache lifetime as possible future work, not an available setting.

events.author: grantmagdanz
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: Later on May 16, grantmagdanz reports that downgrading to 13.3.1 gives their application the behavior they wanted. They prefer fresh data despite slower navigation and ask for a way to disable page-level caching in future versions. This is one participant confirming a workaround in their own application.

events.author: Fredkiss3
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: Fredkiss3 sketches a hypothetical pageTTL setting on May 16 to illustrate a desired cache configuration. The comment explicitly says this is the author's guess, that they are not privy to the Next.js or Vercel plans, and that an official API might look different. The sketch is not evidence that pageTTL is a supported Next.js export.

events.author: Fredkiss3
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On May 17, Fredkiss3 proposes a custom link that calls router.push followed by router.refresh inside startTransition. The stated tradeoff is clearing the client cache and requiring a server round trip even for static pages; startTransition is intended to keep the interface responsive during navigation. This is a suggested workaround, not proof that every application avoids extra requests.

events.author: zuinqstudio-admin
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: In response on May 17, zuinqstudio-admin says they tried the suggested refresh approach but their component refreshes twice and makes two API fetches. They intend to try the earlier downgrade suggestion. This reports a problem with the workaround in their application; it does not report that they already completed or validated the downgrade.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On July 17, timneutkens corrects the suggestion that no Next.js team member has engaged: both Sebastian and Tim have replied. The team is evaluating feedback, and some reported cases appear to need more specific documentation and examples rather than a behavioral change. This comment does not classify every report as a documentation problem.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On August 10, timneutkens says all comments have been read and categorized, and the team is evaluating the thirty-second router cache and configurability. A new explanation and feedback thread is planned. The author explicitly clarifies that the outdated labels were a way to track processed comments, not a claim that their content had become obsolete.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On August 11, timneutkens says the write-up covers about half the identified topics so far. They expect to finish that part on Monday and will share the new issue once it exists. This is a progress report and expectation, not a published resolution.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On August 15 in the morning, timneutkens reports that the explanation is close to completion and still needs review by sebmarkbage later that day. The comment does not publish the write-up or announce approval of a new cache configuration.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On August 15 in the evening, timneutkens links discussion 54075 as the new explanation. It covers mutations, partial rendering, back and forward navigation, and behavior resembling useSWR or react-query, then asks for feedback on reducing the thirty-second interval to zero. Participants are asked to read it before responding. This is publication of a discussion, not a release announcement.

events.author: timneutkens
events.original_hash_scope: GitHub API body field, UTF-8, no newline normalization
events.text: On August 16, timneutkens says issue 42991 will be closed and locked in favor of the newly linked discussion so readers can consider its explanation and questions and continue resolving the matter there. Closure is a move of the discussion, not a statement that every user's problem has been fixed.

limitations: No private team membership, approval, deletion or revocation event is asserted.
The corpus contains faithful human paraphrases, not verbatim community data; this changes the extraction problem.
The linked discussion 54075 is not ingested; only the publication and stated scope of that discussion are known here.
A merged PR proves integration, not successful deployment for all participants.
No claim is made about current Next.js behavior in 2026.
The case represents routine developer support and upgrade work, not a household calendar deployment.
